subject: Taxes
title: The Magna Carta and Tax Consent
description: A 60-second lesson on The Magna Carta and Tax Consent.

hook.text: In 1215, English barons forced King John to sign the Magna Carta. Its key demand: no taxes without consent.

buildup.text: King John had taxed nobles ruthlessly to fund wars. They rebelled not against taxation, but against arbitrary taxation.

discovery.text: Clause 12 required the king to consult a council before levying new taxes. It was the seed of parliamentary democracy.

twist.text: The Magna Carta was annulled by the Pope within weeks. But the idea survived: consent to taxation became sacred.

climax.text: 'No taxation without representation' traces back to this document. Democracy grew from a tax dispute.

punchline.text: A tax revolt in 1215 planted the seed of modern democracy.

quiz.question: What was the Magna Carta's key demand regarding taxes?
